newsitem.title: ITALY: S&P affirms BNL ratings, longterm outlook negative.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms BNL ratings, longterm outlook negative.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Standard & Poors said on Tuesday it affirmed its 'A-/A-2' counterparty ratings of Italy's Banca Nazionale del Lavoro SpA (BNL), revising its outlook on the bank's long-term rating to negative from stable.
S&P said in a statement received in Milan that BNL's ratings reflect the bank's importance to the Italian banking system and its ultimate ownership by the Italian Treasury.

"Historically, BNL has suffered from poor operating performances, high costs, mediocre asset quality, and a weak capital base compared with its main domestic and international peers...but costs seem to have been stabilised thanks to a worldwide reorganisation of the group carried out in recent years," S&P said.

"The negative outlook primarily reflects the possibility of privatisation, which would lead Standard and Poor's to base its ratings on BNL's stand-alone situation to a greater extent than in the past," it said.

S&P said the bank's poor operating performances, the uncertainties surrounding current trends in its asset quality, and its weak position in an increasingly competitive market would deserve lower ratings than the current ones.
"The state's continued involvement is vital to the bank's current ratings.

"These ratings could thus be lowered if the bank were privatised before its financial performance had improved significantly. The ratings could also be subject to review if there were a major decline in the bank's situation due, for instance, to asset quality problems stemming from its large real estate exposure," the S&P statement said.
